title: Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
content:
Apple will now let Siri AI perform actions across third-party apps. As part of the iOS 27.3 update rolling out on Tuesday, Apple announced developers can now integrate Siri AI’s new features in “all apps,” allowing the voice assistant to draw on a user’s personal context, process natural language prompts, and use on-screen awareness to complete requests.
Apple starts giving Siri AI access to third-party apps
Siri AI will soon be able to carry out tasks across a wider range of apps.
The update, which is rolling out as part of a Developer Preview, also adds a new “app skills” feature that third-party developers can create to combine several tasks into a single action. In Apple’s developer documentation, the company says users won’t have to mention an app’s name in their request while it’s in the foreground, during a Live Activity, or in a conversation with Siri AI about the app.
“For example, a person might request a ride with a ride share app, follow updates to the app’s Live Activity while they wait for their ride to arrive, then request to move the pickup location to a different address by saying ‘Hey Siri, change my ride pickup to a new address,’” Apple says. As noted by 9to5Mac, Apple previously made a smaller set of features available to third-party developers.
Apple is bringing Siri AI’s expanded capabilities to its own apps as well, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather apps. “Users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year,” according to Apple. The company notes that users can ask Siri AI what it can do in each app.

report.summary: Apple's iOS 27.3 developer preview opens Siri AI to third-party apps, adding contextual actions, on-screen awareness, and developer-defined 'app skills' for multi-step tasks.
report.background: Apple has been under pressure to modernize Siri as Google Assistant, Amazon Alexa, and generative AI chatbots became more capable. Apple Intelligence, announced in 2024, brought AI features to iPhone but initially kept Siri's third-party app control narrow, mostly through SiriKit intents and Shortcuts. Meanwhile, the industry is shifting toward agentic assistants that can understand context, see the screen, and complete tasks across apps rather than just answer questions. Opening Siri AI to all apps is Apple's move to turn the assistant into an OS-level action layer and to keep its ecosystem competitive with Android's Gemini integrations and third-party AI agents. The developer preview also signals that Apple wants app makers to build around Siri rather than bypass it.
key_points: The iOS 27.3 developer preview lets any third-party app integrate Siri AI, which can use personal context, natural-language prompts, and on-screen awareness to carry out requests inside apps. This expands Siri beyond the limited feature set Apple previously offered developers.

A new 'app skills' feature lets developers combine several tasks into a single action. Users also won't need to name an app when it's in the foreground, running a Live Activity, or being discussed with Siri AI, making interactions feel more natural.

Apple is extending the same capabilities to its own apps, including Calendar, Mail, Maps, Messages, Photos, Reminders, Safari, and Weather. Apple's examples include finding a coffee shop visited last week or archiving files not opened in over a year.

The rollout is a developer preview, not an immediate consumer launch, and follows earlier, smaller third-party integrations. Apple says users can ask Siri AI what it can do in each app, which may help discovery but also highlights the need for clear permissions and predictable behavior.
report.impact: This makes Siri a platform-level agent rather than a voice command layer, raising competitive pressure on Google, Amazon, and third-party AI assistant startups. Developers gain a new distribution channel for app actions, but must adopt Apple's frameworks, design safe multi-step skills, and handle privacy-sensitive context. For regular users, the appeal is hands-free control across apps, such as changing a ride pickup, archiving old files, or finding a past location, without jumping between apps. The risks are mis-triggered actions, opaque data use, and over-permissioned apps. Apple's challenge will be balancing convenience with trust, especially as assistants act on users' behalf.
report.tools: Developers should watch Apple's App Intents framework and SiriKit documentation, plus the new 'app skills' APIs in the iOS 27.3 developer preview. Apple Shortcuts remains a practical way to prototype multi-step actions. For cross-platform comparison, study Android's Gemini extensions and Amazon's Alexa Skills Kit. Open-source agent frameworks such as LangGraph and OpenAI's function-calling patterns can help teams design multi-step app actions, though Apple's ecosystem requires native integration.
